title: Hello, Vow
intro: Start with output and variables. You will print values, store them with let, and drop them into text with ${name}. Plain braces in a string stay as written, which makes templates and JSON easy to type.

title: Functions without type noise
intro: Vow infers every type, so you never write one. A function that never says return gives back its last line, and every function works on any type that fits. Small unnamed functions look like x => x * 2.

title: Lists, maps and loops
intro: Loop over lists with for, or reach for the built-in fold, map, filter and sort. Maps use string keys, and keys(m) lists them in the order you added them.

title: No nulls, no exceptions
intro: Anything that can fail returns a Result: ok(value) or err(message). match handles both cases, and Vow refuses to run a program that ignores one. Inside a function, ? unwraps ok or hands the err back to the caller.

title: Structs and matching
intro: A struct is a record with named fields. Here you sort a cart by price with sortBy, then use match on plain values, with _ catching everything else.

title: Text and patterns
intro: words splits on any whitespace. Regular expressions go in backtick strings, so nothing needs escaping, and matches, find, findAll and replaceAll cover the usual jobs.

title: Working with JSON
intro: parseJson returns a Result, so bad input is handled up front. field reads a key and gives null instead of crashing when it is missing, jsonList walks arrays, and toJson turns Vow values back into JSON text.

title: Contracts
intro: expects says what callers must guarantee and ensures says what a function promises back. Vow proves some broken calls wrong before the program runs, and at runtime a broken contract stops the program and says whether the bug is in the caller or the function. The last call in this lesson fails on purpose so you can see that message.

title: Capabilities
intro: A function that touches the network, files or environment has to say so with uses net, uses fs or uses env. Reading a signature tells you exactly what that code can reach. In the playground, network calls always fail safely.

title: Modules
intro: Split a program across files with import "./shapes.vow" as shapes, then call shapes.area(r). A module holds functions and structs, and names starting with _ stay private. Modules run in the command-line tool, not in the browser playground.

title: Running Vow on your computer
intro: You need Node.js 20 or newer. Install Vow with npm install -g github:JakeBurwick/vow, then run any program with vow program.vow. Vow compiles to JavaScript, so programs run fast, and the flags below check code, limit what it can touch, and make randomness repeatable.
commands: only let the program touch ./data, checked before it runs
only let it call one host
use the interpreter instead of the compiler

title: Project: a grade report
intro: This program puts the earlier lessons together. It parses CSV text into structs, skips a bad row with a Result instead of crashing, averages the scores, assigns letter grades and prints a sorted table.
